found.quote: All work submitted by students for assessment is accepted on the understanding that it is the student's own effort.
Students must not use generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools or AI-powered websites in ways which breach assessment instructions, for example to generate content, answers, or references.
Students must not use generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools or AI-powered websites in ways which breach assessment instructions
Schools will advise students of their specific rules and in assessment specifications, where appropriate.
Schools will advise students of their specific rules and in assessment specifications, where appropriate.
Where the use of AI is permitted, it must be verified and appropriately referenced in the work for transparency, with details of how it was used being provided.
If information or ideas are obtained from any source (including GenAI), those sources must be acknowledged according to the appropriate convention in that subject
Where the use of AI is permitted, it must be verified and appropriately referenced in the work for transparency
Any failure to acknowledge adequately or to cite properly other sources in submitted work is plagiarism.
Plagiarism is defined as the submission or presentation of work, in any form, which is not one's own, without proper acknowledgement of the source(s).
the School may arrange an Exploratory Interview with the student in order to assess their understanding of the work they have submitted.
The student has the right of appeal to the Senate Assessors for Student Conduct in respect of any penalty imposed by the Head of School.
There does not need to be any deliberate attempt to deceive.
The University reserves the right to use University-approved systems, such as similarity checking software, to assist with the detection of plagiarism or generative AI misuse
The Head of School may reduce the grade by one or more bands, down to grade H. If a resubmission is permitted and available, the resubmission will be capped at the pass mark
